problem:
The matrix $D$ is given below. Let ${d}_{1}$, ${d}_{2}$, and ${d}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $D.$ Determine if $B=\text{{}{d}_{1},{d}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(D).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${d}_{2}={x}_{1}{d}_{1}+{x}_{3}{d}_{3}.$ 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $A$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{16}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $3$rd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(D)$ is ${{d}_{1},{d}_{3}},$ that is to say,

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Now, since the $2$nd column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express ${d}_{2}$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 24\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{d}_{2}}={{(-6)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{d}_{1}}+{{(0)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{3}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{d}_{3}}.
$$

This gives us ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}=-6\cdot 0=0.$
